item.title: Trinket 0.1.0 Preview (10)
item.description:
### Added
- Workflow packages can receive signed live updates with Pinned or Automatic policies; updates needing setup keep the current workflow usable until setup is complete. Workflows settings exposes publisher review, policy controls, release notes and applied update history. - A workflow can read a folder you allow, read-only, at /workspace inside its box. Allow folders on the workflow page. A run that names another folder asks for your approval. Name the folder with trinket run --folder, or with folder_path on the workflow MCP tool. - App startup preserves pre-migration database checkpoints across failed upgrades and retries, and offers Retry Startup while retaining credential-key protections. - Show configured package and workflow labels, with input names below run headings. - Runs started with a JSON object input show its title or text field as their title, so Git message checks are named in the run list. - When the CLI or an MCP client changes a package in a way that touches a configured secret, sign-in or write-back folder, Trinket asks for your approval on the Packages page. Agents read the answer with the get_access_request tool. - Packages can declare their update source and default channel; trusted signed archives configure updates while preserving pins, channels, opt-outs and local packages. - Workflow authors can create change fragments and prepare reviewed release notes and version plans with the Bun release utility.
### Changed
- Updates download about half as much, and Trinket takes about 260 MB less disk space. - In the Settings window, Models, MCP Servers and Workflows use macOS system type, colors and grouped sections, so they match General. - CLI and MCP runs no longer write a revision back to their input file, and the MCP workflow tools drop input_path. - Workflow submissions receive a retryable update-pending response while an app restart waits for accepted workflows and package installs to finish. - The engine and workflow boxes now run on Bun 1.4.4.
### Fixed
- Switching workflows and collapsing sidebar folders clears the previous selection highlight without leaving an overlapping row. - Active workflows keep their settings and credentials during updates or removal; unused data is cleaned up when they finish. - Checking for updates when none is available no longer shows a red error in Settings or cancels a quit that waits for active workflows.
### Security
- A saved provider key or sign-in is sent only to the host it was saved for. Provider settings can no longer add request headers or name an environment key. - Only Trinket.app can change settings, secrets, sign-ins, write-back folders and updates. The CLI, MCP clients and any process that reads engine.json can still run workflows, read results and install packages.
### Migration
Configure a write-back destination for the revision's kind, or start the run from Trinket.app to revise the file in place.
